chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a pigeon slaughtered in the hill area, he said: A muhrim must not eat it. If it is brought into Makkah, a person who is not in ihram may eat it in Makkah. But if it is brought into the Haram alive and then slaughtered in the Haram, he must not eat it, because it was slaughtered after it had reached its place of safety.

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary around Makkah with special legal protections
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred sanctuary of the Haram
key_terms.الْمُحِلُّ: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.مَأْمَنَهُ: its place of safety or sanctuary where it is protected
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim or a non-muhrim eat a pigeon slaughtered outside the Haram if it is brought into Makkah or slaughtered after entering the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a hunted pigeon slaughtered outside the Haram and later brought into Makkah or the Haram. It distinguishes between the state of ihram and non-ihram, and between slaughter before entering the Haram and slaughter after the animal has entered the sanctuary and reached its protected refuge.
